manifest_scheme.problem: CLAUDE_HANDOVER.md and CLAUDE_HANDOVER.json are two of the 26 authorized candidate paths, and a complete manifest was required to list SHA256 for all 26 paths inside these two files (no separate manifest file). A file cannot contain its own final hash (writing the hash changes the file, which changes the hash - unterminating). Strict MUTUAL embedding (each file containing the other's final hash) is equally impossible for the same reason: finalizing file A requires file B's final hash, and finalizing file B requires file A's final hash - neither can be finalized first.
manifest_scheme.resolution: Sequential (non-mutual) finalization, chosen from the authorized alternatives ('or another clearly non-recursive cross-manifest arrangement'). Order: (1) CLAUDE_HANDOVER.json is finalized FIRST. It contains SHA256 + byte size for all 24 non-evidence implementation files (18 ADD + 6 MODIFY) and does NOT reference either handover file's own hash - this makes the JSON's content independent of anything not yet known, so it can be finalized without circularity. (2) CLAUDE_HANDOVER.json's own SHA256 is computed once it is finalized. (3) CLAUDE_HANDOVER.md is finalized SECOND. It contains the same 24 implementation-file hashes PLUS the now-known final SHA256 of CLAUDE_HANDOVER.json (safe, because JSON is already frozen and will not be edited again). (4) CLAUDE_HANDOVER.md's own SHA256 is computed after it is finalized, but is NOT embedded in JSON (doing so would require re-finalizing JSON, which would change the JSON hash already recorded inside MD, reintroducing the exact circularity being avoided) and is NOT embedded in MD itself (self-reference). Instead MD's final SHA256 is reported directly in Claude's chat completion response for this correction round, where the Windows Operator can independently recompute and compare it with sha256sum - matching the brief's own statement that 'The Windows Operator will independently hash all 26 files anyway.'
manifest_scheme.consequence: JSON is the 'inner' document (frozen first, its hash is a fact MD can safely cite). MD is the 'outer' document (frozen last, cites JSON's hash, and its own hash exists only outside both files - in the chat record and in the Operator's own independent re-hash).
